newsitem.title: USA: Dole hits foreign funds to Clinton's party.
newsitem.headline: Dole hits foreign funds to Clinton's party.

text.p: Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole delivered an all-day assault on President Bill Clinton on Friday for not explaining alleged improper foreign campaign contributions to Democrats, contending the money trail leads right to his White House office.

Dole and aides honed in on the campaign financing issue first in Albuquerque, New Mexico, in Denver and then in Wichita in his home state of Kansas on a swing eastward from California and his Wednesday debate with Clinton.

In Albuquerque, he told the New Mexico rally he wanted to restore values to the White House instead of "slippery liberalism" as he heated up his attack with time running short before the Nov. 5 election.

"Follow the money," Dole intoned in Albuquerque, claiming the foreign contributions would lead to the White House although he gave no evidence to substantiate the innuendo that Clinton was involved or did anything wrong.

In recent days, Dole's new get-tough tactics have hit hard at alleged "scandals" and ethical lapses he sees at the White House -- underscoring reports about questionable contributions from people associated with Indonesian, South Korean and other foreign interests into the Democratic Party.

In Kansas, one of the states where he leads Clinton handily, Dole told a noisy airport rally that "we're going to cut off some of this foreign money coming its way to the Democratic National Committee."

He linked purported foreign contributions to other big Democratic contributors. "They've got the trial lawyers and they've got the labour bosses and they've got the Hollywwod elite and now they're getting foreign aid from Indonesia and India and a few other countries," Dole charged as the crowd booed.
Earlier in Denver, Dole hammered away at the foreign contribution issue before several thousand cheering students at a middle school who seemed to be unaware of the issue.
Dole said federal laws should be changed to bar foreigners from making contributions. Non-citizens now are generally barred from giving money for political campaigns but there are exceptions.

He charged that Democrats are running negative ads against him and "a lot of those ads that are being run are probably being paid for with some of this foreign money. I say it is time to say if you are not a citizen you can't contribute to a political campaign in the United States of America and it is time we changed the law."
"This abuse of the political process must stop and if I'm president of the United States it is going to stop," Dole said.

In New Mexico, Dole said, "Every day we have a new scandal involving the foreign corruption of America. Our elections are not for sale to some foreign influence or some foreign interest. This is the United States of America."

"Make no mistake about it, a public office is a public trust. And it's time to restore that trust in America and it's time to return values to America in exchange for slippery liberalism in the Clinton administration and bring back common sense and integrity to the White House," he said.
